transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

Yes — on many Beko washer-dryers, that is normal. They use a small continuous flow of cold water during drying to condense moisture out of the warm air, then pump that water away. So hearing water enter and drain during a dry-only programme does not, by itself, mean there is a fault. 1. Make sure the cold-water tap is fully on and the inlet hose is not kinked. The drying system may rely on that water flow.
2. Check the drain hose behind the machine is not squashed or kinked. Condensed water has to be pumped away continuously.
3. Fluff or debris there can restrict the water used during drying. During that drying programme, does the drum/clothing become warm and does it eventually dry, or is it staying cold or leaving the load wet?

Thank you. Yes, the clothes come out dry at the end of the cycle, and the drying time counts down normally with no error codes. I haven't checked the hoses yet, but there's no leak on the floor. Is this really normal, or is it a sign it's been built to wear out early?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes — with the results you describe, this is really normal operation, not evidence that it is deliberately wearing itself out early. A water-cooled condenser washer-dryer uses a controlled trickle of cold water during drying to remove moisture from the warm air, then sends that water to the drain. It can therefore sound as though it is filling and pumping for much of the dry cycle. The reassuring signs are that it dries the clothes, completes and counts down normally, has no error code, and there is no leak. A fault in that system would more usually show as poor/very slow drying, an error, water backing up or a leak. When convenient, just check the cold-water tap is fully open and the inlet and drain hoses have not been trapped or kinked behind the machine. That is preventative rather than because your symptoms point to a fault. If it starts leaving clothes damp, takes much longer than usual, shows an error or leaks, then the water supply, drain path/pump filter and condensation path would need checking. On the information so far, no repair or part replacement is indicated.
